parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans identity or same-sex conduct survives (2024 court decision), and the 2011 HIV law plus constitutional health care give one operative, traveller-facing protection. But the combined regime shows state-tolerated hostility toward visible LGBTQ presence (signage crackdowns, 2006 venue closures, 2012 parade arrests), deep social hostility (69%/5% polls, religious influence), zero general non-discrimination protection, no documented hate-crime recourse, and no legal recognition route. Worst documented feature is tier 2–3: state-tolerated targeting of visibility plus societal hostility with thin recourse. Trans-specific border, custody, facility and violence data are thin, requiring conservative structural extrapolation. No tier-1 universal exposure (no birth-sex facility rule, no mandatory document scrutiny) is documented, but absence of such records in a thinly documented jurisdiction is not safety.

entry_documents.exposure: No standing legal gender recognition domestically; whether foreign passport markers are questioned at entry is not documented. A visitor's home-issued documents are the operative papers.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. No border policy accepting or rejecting mismatched markers appears in the sources.
entry_documents.interaction: A document/presentation mismatch could in principle trigger questioning, then public-order attention given documented hostility to visible LGBTQ presence; this chain is plausible but unevidenced.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Historical police harassment of LGBTQ venues (2006) and arrest of Pride marchers (2012); state crackdowns on visible LGBTQ signage. No trans-specific custody or arrest record exists.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No criminalisation of same-sex conduct or trans expression survives the 2024 ruling; the former 'decorum' offence was repealed in 1997.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Police hostility documented against LGBTQ visibility could reach a visibly trans or outed visitor during any stop, but no documented arrest pathway for trans visitors exists.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No facility, custody-placement or strip-search rule by birth sex is documented at any level. Only capital-localised incidents appear; all other content is national.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Not documented. Whether conditions differ outside the capital is unevidenced expectation only.

care_services.exposure: No general non-discrimination duty in health care beyond the HIV sector; LGBTQ health programming is NGO-run and HIV-focused, leaving gaps for transition-related or routine needs.
care_services.protection: Constitutional right to health care, plus the 2011 HIV/AIDS law prohibiting discrimination on sexual orientation and gender identity in that sector — operative and traveller-facing.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing emergency or routine care is covered by the constitutional right; whether the HIV-law shield extends beyond HIV contexts is uncertain.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Government crackdowns on visible LGBTQ signage, sometimes with religious leaders; heavyweight Catholic/evangelical influence; 69% poll backing criminalisation of same-sex relations; 5% support for legal gender change; organised domestic opposition (ambassador backlash, expulsion petition).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Constitutional court removed remaining sodomy provisions in 2024; officials addressed a 2017 regional LGBT conference; the country accepted UPR-style SOGI/intersex recommendations.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State and religious threat-framing of visibility raises both the probability of confrontation and the odds police respond unsympathetically if a trans visitor is outed.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. Nothing addresses a travelling parent with a minor, family-law treatment of trans guardians, or age-dependent rules for children.
minors_guardians.interaction: Not documented. A trans adult travelling with a minor would fall under the same undocumented border and social climate, with family-facing hostility unassessed.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence, killing or assault record exists in the dossier. Documented items are dated (2006, 2012) or concern an ambassador; an organised opposition climate is shown. No hate-crime provision or sentencing enhancement is documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Not documented. No evidence of prosecution of anti-trans attackers.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: In a climate where religious and political figures attack LGBTQ visibility, a street assault on an outed visitor could meet indifference; whether police would assist is unevidenced.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No non-discrimination remedy in employment, housing, services or accommodations; no standing gender-recognition procedure; regional advisory opinion unimplemented; no documented hate-crime recourse.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Health-sector discrimination ban (2011 law) with enforcement unspecified; regional human rights court advisory opinion; constitutional court willingness to strike rights-restrictive provisions (2024).
remedies_unknowns.interaction: A visitor denied service or harassed has no documented domestic avenue; the only functioning shield is health-sector, and its reach beyond HIV contexts is uncertain.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this case: Vellandra has a universal, state-imposed entry register barring transgender visitors with routine enforcement. This dossier documents no entry bar, no registration, no mandatory reporting of trans guests, and no criminalisation. Its hostility is societal and visibility-targeted rather than a mechanical exclusion regime, so it sits well above 0.35.

Similar in kind but different in mechanism: Kestrel Isles documents border secondary screening and discretionary refusal of admission — a direct traveller-facing exposure. This dossier documents no such border practice (open question, not exposure), but adds deeper documented social hostility, state crackdowns on visibility and near-total absence of recourse. Roughly comparable; the undocumented border question here is offset by the documented hostile climate.

Materially below this case: Meridia documents trained border officers, respectful inspection, a working appeals tribunal and compensation for unlawful detention. This dossier documents no trained-officer regime, no complaints tribunal, no compensation practice, and instead shows state-tolerated hostility toward LGBTQ visibility plus zero general anti-discrimination protection. The absence of criminalisation alone cannot reach 0.75.

Similar tier: Aldermere's health-ministry bulletin limits gender-related care for non-residents, a universal exposure for care-seeking visitors, with weak remedies. This dossier lacks that care barrier (constitutionally guaranteed care plus an SOGI non-discrimination statute in health), so it is somewhat better on care, but lacks even the commission-based complaint route Aldermere offers elsewhere; net position is close.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime offers a visitor no criminalisation path and one real protection — constitutionally guaranteed health care reinforced by the 2011 SOGI non-discrimination provision in the HIV sector — alongside a constitutional court willing to strike rights-restrictive provisions. Against that: no general non-discrimination protection anywhere else, no documented hate-crime recourse, no legal recognition procedure, documented state-tolerated crackdowns on visible LGBTQ presence, historical police harassment of LGBTQ venues and a Pride parade, and a social climate (69% backing criminalisation of same-sex relations, 5% backing trans legal change, organised religious opposition) hostile to visibility. Trans-specific border, custody and violence evidence is thin, so structural signals govern: hostility is real, remedies for a visitor are essentially absent, but no imprisonment pathway for an outed trans visitor is documented. Adult-alone and adult-with-minor travellers face the same undocumented border position; family-specific exposure is simply unassessed.
